User Story: As assigned Technical Support Staff, I want to be notified when the Event Coordinator rejects an alternative arrangement so I can follow up.
Acceptance Criteria: When an assigned coordinator rejects a replacement, the system stores an in-app notification for assigned Technical Support Staff and emails the stored notification after the rejection transaction commits.
Test Scenario: Happy: assigned staff receives the rejection notification by in-app record and email; error: a transaction that does not commit must not trigger notification email; boundary: notification identifies the rejected outcome, event, reservation, and assigned recipient.
Pre-Conditions: An affected reservation has a pending replacement suggestion and assigned Technical Support IDs.
Test Steps: Arrange a pending issue with one assigned support recipient; reject the suggestion; assert the notification content/recipient and email delivery after COMMIT.
Test Data: Support user 6; event 401; reservation 301; original asset MIC-001; outcome rejected.
Expected Results: Assigned Technical Support Staff learns that the alternative was rejected and is asked to follow up; the reservation remains unchanged and open.
Test Details: Test 'AC3/AC4 - rejects an offer, preserves the reservation, and notifies assigned support staff' checks recipient, event/type/title/message/details, unchanged reservation, open issue and email-after-COMMIT behavior. Missing, misdirected, wrong-outcome or premature notification fails assertions. Database and email provider are represented by test doubles.

User Story: As assigned Technical Support Staff, I want to be notified when the Event Coordinator approves an alternative arrangement so I know the reservation has been updated.
Acceptance Criteria: After an assigned coordinator accepts a replacement, the system stores an in-app notification for assigned Technical Support Staff and emails the stored notification after the reservation transaction commits.
Test Scenario: Happy: assigned staff receives an acceptance notification by in-app record and email; error: a transaction that does not commit must not trigger notification email; boundary: notification is scoped to assigned support staff and includes the affected event/reservation.
Pre-Conditions: An affected reservation has a pending replacement suggestion and assigned Technical Support IDs.
Test Steps: Arrange a pending issue with one assigned support recipient; accept the replacement; assert the notification content/recipient and email call after COMMIT.
Test Data: Support user 6; event 401; reservation 301; original asset MIC-001; outcome accepted.
Expected Results: Assigned Technical Support Staff receives the stored acceptance notification and its email copy only after the reservation update commits.
Test Details: Test 'AC3 - accepts a still-available offer and transfers the reservation quantity' inspects notification recipient, event, type, title, message, issue/reservation details, and verifies email delivery starts after COMMIT. Omitting or misrouting the notification or emailing before commit fails the assertion. Database writes are simulated with a query recorder.

User Story: As Technical Support Staff, I want failed reservation data loads to be clearly distinguished from empty results.
Acceptance Criteria: When reservation loading fails, the dashboard displays an error and does not claim there are no upcoming or affected reservations.
Test Scenario: Happy: successful empty results still show the empty state; error: failed API response shows unavailable messaging; boundary: both affected and confirmed reservation sections avoid false empty claims.
Pre-Conditions: The reservation endpoint returns a database-update-required error while other dashboard APIs still load.
Test Steps: Arrange a rejected reservation API request; open the reservation tab; assert error and unavailable messages and verify no empty-state claims.
Test Data: 503 DATABASE_UPDATE_REQUIRED response.
Expected Results: Staff can distinguish database failure from a genuinely empty reservation queue.
Test Details: AC1 error case is tested through the user-facing dashboard. A regression that renders 'No upcoming...' on rejection fails the assertions. The successful no-alternative/empty fixtures preserve the genuine empty-state branch.

User Story: As Technical Support Staff, I want every future reservation using unavailable equipment flagged so I can arrange an acceptable replacement.
Acceptance Criteria: Marking equipment unavailable records each affected future reservation, checks replacement stock for its event slot, and keeps the issue open when no alternative is available.
Test Scenario: Happy: each affected reservation gets its own issue and coordinator/support notifications; error: no eligible stock is explicitly recorded rather than silently closing the issue; boundary: multiple reservations for different events are all processed.
Pre-Conditions: Two future reservations use the asset; candidate lookup returns no eligible stock.
Test Steps: Arrange two affected reservation rows; act by marking their shared equipment unavailable; assert both issue IDs, no-alternative states, notifications, and committed status update.
Test Data: Reservations 301 and 302; separate event/coordinator/support identities; zero eligible alternatives.
Expected Results: Both reservations remain visible for follow-up with distinct issue records; the equipment status transition is still committed.
Test Details: AC1 happy and no-alternative/error cases plus the multiple-reservation boundary are covered. Assertions fail if the loop drops an affected booking, notification recipients are omitted, or no-alternative state is not persisted. Database behavior is represented by a query recorder; live PostgreSQL concurrency is not covered.

User Story: As Technical Support Staff, I want to select and send an eligible replacement to the Event Coordinator.
Acceptance Criteria: A staff-selected replacement must be operational, Available, sufficient for the full affected quantity, and available for the exact event slot; stale or malformed selections are rejected.
Test Scenario: Happy: a valid alternative is locked, rechecked, persisted and sent to the coordinator; error: insufficient/stale stock and malformed bodies are rejected; boundary: validation is repeated after initial issue creation and only exact slot coverage qualifies.
Pre-Conditions: An open affected reservation records its original asset, slot, quantity and assigned coordinator; alternative stock may change before suggestion.
Test Steps: Submit one valid and one stale selection and invalid API payloads; assert the exact replacement ID, notification and rollback behavior.
Test Data: Issue 71 requires two units from 09:00-12:00; replacement asset 93 has either two available units or no eligible stock.
Expected Results: A valid suggestion becomes pending and notifies the coordinator; stale/invalid suggestions create no pending offer.
Test Details: AC2 happy, error, and exact-slot boundary cases are covered by service and controller tests. Lock/recheck ordering, stored IDs, notification details, rollback, and zero calls for invalid bodies fail if a plausible check is removed. Test doubles record SQL; actual row-lock behavior is not exercised.

User Story: As an Event Coordinator, I want to accept or reject a replacement suggestion so the reservation reflects my decision.
Acceptance Criteria: Acceptance rechecks replacement stock, transfers the affected quantity, and resolves the issue; rejection preserves the original allocation and leaves the issue open for staff follow-up.
Test Scenario: Happy: an eligible offer is accepted and the reservation quantity is transferred; error: a stale offer cannot be accepted and reports failure; boundary: rejection does not alter reservation items, and event/coordinator ownership must match.
Pre-Conditions: The affected reservation has a pending offer and is accessed by its assigned coordinator.
Test Steps: Arrange pending offers; act by accepting, rejecting, or accepting after stock loss; assert item writes, issue status and notification outcome.
Test Data: Reservation 301; original inventory 92; suggested inventory 93; quantity 2; assigned event 401/coordinator 5.
Expected Results: Acceptance merges quantity onto replacement and resolves the issue; rejection keeps reservation unchanged and issue open; stale acceptance rolls back.
Test Details: AC3 happy, rejection/error, and stale-stock boundary cases are covered. Assertions fail if acceptance skips revalidation or quantity transfer, rejection deletes the original allocation, or frontend sends the wrong decision. SQL is query-recorded; PostgreSQL locking and email delivery are not exercised.

User Story: As Technical Support Staff and Event Coordinator, I want replacement options and decisions visible in the relevant dashboards.
Acceptance Criteria: Support can send a selected alternative or see an explicit no-stock state; the coordinator can accept/reject a pending offer and sees errors when a decision fails.
Test Scenario: Happy: support sends an eligible selection and the coordinator accepts/rejects; error: no alternatives and failed API decisions are surfaced; boundary: no selector is shown without stock and a rejected issue stays in follow-up.
Pre-Conditions: Dashboard API fixtures provide one affected issue with stock, one without stock, and one pending coordinator offer.
Test Steps: Arrange user-facing dashboard routes; select and submit replacement; accept/reject or simulate an API failure; assert visible state and API payload.
Test Data: Alternative asset 92; pending issue 71; failure message identifies stock no longer available.
Expected Results: The affected reservation action is visible, coordinator decisions are persisted through the API, and failure/no-stock states do not look successful.
Test Details: Tests cover happy submit/decision, no-alternative and API-error cases, and unresolved pending state. Accessible control and message assertions fail for a missing action, false success, or wrong payload; all test blocks were inspected.

User Story: As Technical Support Staff, scan equipment availability month by month without crowded date headers.
Acceptance Criteria: The calendar uses a readable seven-column month grid; every in-range unscheduled date is explicitly Available, while scheduled blocked periods remain Unavailable.
Test Scenario: Happy: scheduled availability and event details are readable in a seven-column month grid; error: an unscheduled date must not display a dash or imply unknown state; boundary: past dates and offsets at/after the 90-day horizon are outside the visible range.
Pre-Conditions: Equipment has one scheduled window and missing windows on other dates in the current month; fixture dates are relative to today.
Test Steps: Arrange a matching inventory item; act by searching it and advancing month-by-month; assert seven weekday headers, Available on unscheduled in-range days, no dash, and the horizon boundary.
Test Data: Scheduled 09:00–17:00; unscheduled dates; horizon offsets 89 and 90.
Expected Results: A clean Sunday-to-Saturday grid labels empty schedule days Available and preserves the rolling horizon.
Test Details: Test: AC1 - searches by ID or name and shows the matched asset calendar separately; AC1 - pages month by month and shows unscheduled in-range dates as available. Happy schedule display, unscheduled-date fallback/error condition, and horizon boundary are covered. A calendar with 31 crowded columns, a dash, wrong status, or out-of-horizon dates fails assertions; tests inspected. No uncovered branch claimed before coverage run.

User Story: As Technical Support Staff, change equipment availability using the status selector and preserve an auditable history.
Acceptance Criteria: Available/Unavailable transitions require the appropriate reason, update inventory only after success, and show status-history dates; marking equipment unavailable records and notifies affected future reservations.
Test Scenario: Happy: both status transitions save with their entered reason and status history has a visible date; error: missing reasons are rejected and failed transitions do not create a success state; boundary: a conflicting concurrent status transition rolls back and records no audit or affected issue.
Pre-Conditions: The dashboard loads an available and an unavailable equipment item; unavailable-transition endpoint receives a future reservation fixture.
Test Steps: Arrange the dashboard and audit fixtures; act by selecting each status and submitting its reason; assert API payloads, status, date, and affected-reservation notification.
Test Data: Unavailable reason 'Battery failed inspection'; repair reason 'Screen replaced'; one future affected reservation; status history 10 Oct 2026.
Expected Results: The status dropdown controls the audited flows; dates are visible; affected reservations are flagged; invalid or conflicting writes do not change state.
Test Details: Happy available-to-unavailable and repair transitions, empty-reason error cases, and stale-status conflict boundary are asserted. Each assertion fails for a missing dropdown, absent date, omitted audit/impact write, or success-shaped conflict. Tests inspected; backend database behavior is simulated with a query recorder. Full coverage results are recorded after the coverage command.

User Story: As a developer maintaining database upgrades, preserve cancellation and equipment-review migrations when adding equipment repair history.
Acceptance Criteria: The migration runner applies the cancellation migration, then the equipment-review migration, and appends equipment repair history as the final migration.
Test Scenario: Happy case: the migration runner submits the existing cancellation and equipment-review SQL in order. Boundary case: equipment repair history is the final SQL migration. Error case: migration execution failures are not exercised by this ordering test.
Pre-Conditions: Migration SQL files exist; the PostgreSQL connection is replaced with an in-memory call recorder.
Test Steps: Arrange a fake client; act by invoking migrate(); assert cancellation precedes equipment review and repair history is last.
Test Data: 012-event-cancellation-notifications.sql; 013-equipment-review-affected-items.sql; 012-equipment-repair-history.sql.
Expected Results: Both preserved migrations are applied and the repair-history migration is applied last.
Test Details: Test: test('migration runner preserves cancellation and equipment-review migrations before appending repair history'). Happy path and append-order boundary are covered; migration-error handling is outside this test. A missing call, reversed order, or later migration after repair history makes an assertion fail. The test was inspected and failed before the fix because cancellation was absent.

User Story: As a database maintainer, rerun migration 006 without rejecting existing cancellation or equipment-status notifications.
Acceptance Criteria: Migration 006 notification constraint permits both event_cancelled and equipment_status_changed while retaining all previously accepted types.
Test Scenario: Happy case: both cancellation and equipment-status types are present. Error case: omitted existing types would fail migration when matching rows exist; this test detects omissions from the list. Boundary case: exact accepted type list is asserted.
Pre-Conditions: The SQL migration file is read as text and its notifications_type_check type list is parsed.
Test Steps: Arrange the migration text; act by extracting accepted types; assert the complete expected type sequence including both requested notification types.
Test Data: event_cancelled; equipment_status_changed; all existing change-request, event decision, and safety types.
Expected Results: Migration 006 allows both existing cancellation notifications and equipment-status notifications when rerun.
Test Details: Test: Migration compatibility - preserves event_cancelled and equipment_status_changed notifications. Happy compatibility case and exact-list boundary are asserted; actual database rejection behavior is not exercised here. The test was inspected and failed before the SQL change because event_cancelled was missing; omission of either notification type causes the equality assertion to fail. Exact updated SQL constraint clause: ALTER TABLE notifications ADD CONSTRAINT notifications_type_check CHECK (type IN ('change_request_submitted', 'change_request_approved', 'change_request_rejected', 'event_details_changed', 'event_approved', 'event_rejected', 'safety_check_recorded', 'event_cancelled', 'equipment_status_changed'));

User Story: As a maintainer, protect repair-history records so they are accessed only through the authorised API.
Acceptance Criteria: Enable row-level security on equipment_status_history and revoke direct privileges from anon and authenticated roles.
Test Scenario: Happy case: migration enables RLS and revokes both browser roles. Error case: omission of any access-control statement leaves a direct access path and fails the assertion. Boundary case: role existence is guarded so migration can run where either role is absent.
Pre-Conditions: The migration SQL is read from disk; PostgreSQL is not needed for this static regression check.
Test Steps: Arrange by loading the SQL; act by checking the migration text; assert RLS and each guarded revoke are present.
Test Data: equipment_status_history; anon; authenticated.
Expected Results: RLS is enabled and direct privileges are revoked from anon and authenticated, leaving API-mediated access.
Test Details: Test: AC4 - enables RLS and revokes anon and authenticated access to repair history. The test was inspected and failed before the SQL change because RLS was absent. Missing RLS or either revoke makes an assertion fail. No SQL behavior is uncovered by this static check, though a live database permission test is not included.

User Story: As Technical Support Staff, repair unavailable equipment so it can be reserved for a new reviewed event and retain the resolution note in its history.
Acceptance Criteria: After repair, the asset is eligible for a new reservation and the exact repair resolution note is persisted in equipment_status_history.
Test Scenario: Happy case: repair the unavailable fixture asset through the authenticated API, then reserve it through the real API and verify durable audit and reservation rows. Error cases and boundary cases are outside this one happy-path regression.
Pre-Conditions: RUN_DB_TESTS=1 and a PostgreSQL connection are required; the test creates a random disposable schema, applies real migrations, and removes the schema afterward.
Test Steps: Arrange users, an unavailable asset, a future availability slot, and a fully reviewed event; act by repairing and creating the reservation; assert the reservation and exact repair history record in PostgreSQL.
Test Data: Unavailable one-unit projector; future date at CURRENT_DATE + 30; resolution note 'Replaced the damaged lamp and passed the projection test.'
Expected Results: Repair returns Available; reservation API returns 201 for the exact asset; PostgreSQL contains the available-status history row with the resolution note and staff identity.
Test Details: Test: AC1-AC2 - repaired equipment can be reserved and its resolution note persists in PostgreSQL history. Inspected; the successful API reservation fails if repaired inventory remains ineligible, and the database equality assertions fail if the note, status, or staff identity is not persisted. Happy path only; no error or boundary scenario is included. The test is opt-in and was not run against the configured non-local database.

User Story: As Technical Support Staff, select equipment and view its reservation schedule across relevant dates and times.
Acceptance Criteria: Searching by equipment ID or name shows the matching asset calendar and scheduled time windows without displaying event names or implying unscheduled dates are reserved.
Test Scenario: Happy: matching equipment shows its calendar and scheduled times; error: unmatched catalogue query does not invent a schedule; boundary: unscheduled calendar cells remain explicitly available per the no-schedule rule.
Pre-Conditions: Inventory includes projector and microphone rows with explicit availability records and event names in the test fixture.
Test Steps: Arrange scheduled inventory; act by searching by asset ID or name; assert the matching calendar and schedule are visible and event names are absent.
Test Data: PROJ-001; future scheduled date; 09:00–17:00; Town Hall; unrelated microphone.
Expected Results: The selected asset calendar shows its scheduled window and available/reserved quantities without revealing event names; unscheduled cells retain their normal availability status.
Test Details: Test: AC1 - searches by ID or name and shows the matched asset calendar separately. Inspected; happy selection, hidden event name, and unscheduled-cell behavior are asserted. Error fallback is covered separately by AC1 - distinguishes an empty catalogue from a failed inventory request. A wrong asset match, missing schedule, displayed event name, or incorrect unscheduled status fails assertions.

User Story: As Technical Support Staff, view equipment schedules beyond the original fixed calendar end date.
Acceptance Criteria: The rolling calendar pages through 90 days, includes the last in-range day, excludes past and out-of-range days, and shows only explicit availability windows.
Test Scenario: Happy: scheduled windows inside the horizon appear while paging; error: no schedule is fabricated for absent dates; boundary: yesterday and offset 90 are excluded while offset 89 is included.
Pre-Conditions: Inventory fixture contains scheduled windows at offsets -1, 0, 89 and 90 from today.
Test Steps: Arrange boundary-date inventory; act by opening the calendar and paging forward; assert first-page and final-page headers and explicit scheduled content.
Test Data: Offsets -1, 0, 89 and 90; 14-day page size; 90-day horizon.
Expected Results: The calendar excludes past and day-90 dates, includes today and day 89, and pages through the in-range schedule without filling unscheduled cells as available.
Test Details: Test: AC1 - pages through 90 days of scheduled windows without showing past or out-of-range dates. Inspected; the assertions fail for an incorrect horizon, off-by-one endpoint, absent pagination, or implied free dates. Happy paging, absent-schedule error behavior, and both in-range/out-of-range boundary dates are covered.

User Story: As Technical Support Staff, distinguish available and reserved periods before confirming requests.
Acceptance Criteria: Each scheduled period clearly reports booked and remaining units without displaying event names.
Test Scenario: Happy: free, partly booked and fully reserved windows display availability status and quantities without event names; error: a fully booked window must not appear available; boundary: remaining units transition from positive to zero at stock capacity.
Pre-Conditions: Inventory has one three-unit item with explicit windows and reserved quantities.
Test Steps: Arrange free, partly booked and fully booked windows; act by selecting the item; assert quantities and availability classes while verifying all event names are absent.
Test Data: Quantity 3; reserved quantities 0, 2 and 3; available quantities 3, 1 and 0; event names Town Hall and Gala.
Expected Results: Calendar shows exact stock quantities and availability styling, and never exposes event names.
Test Details: Test: AC2 - never displays event names for reserved calendar windows. The test first failed because Gala appeared on a fully reserved window; it now asserts that both Town Hall and Gala are absent while preserving quantities and status classes. Happy free/partial/full states, event-name disclosure error, and zero-stock boundary are covered.

User Story: As Technical Support Staff, identify periods blocked by equipment maintenance or damage.
Acceptance Criteria: Maintenance/damage windows are marked blocked and display the explicit reason, latest history note fallback, or a clear generic unavailability reason.
Test Scenario: Happy: explicit damage reason is displayed; error/fallback: missing explicit reason uses latest unavailable history note, then generic unavailable text; boundary: even a schedule marked Available remains blocked when the equipment status is unavailable.
Pre-Conditions: Inventory includes a maintenance item with an explicit reason, an unavailable item with history-only reason, and a legacy unavailable item without history.
Test Steps: Arrange each blocked-reason source; act by searching the equipment; assert every window has blocked text and blocked styling.
Test Data: Damage: cracked lens; history-only unavailable note; legacy unavailable item with no note.
Expected Results: All blocked windows are visibly distinguished and explain the reason without leaking them into the available state.
Test Details: Test: AC3 - marks maintenance windows blocked and displays the recorded damage reason. Inspected; assertions fail if an unavailable item is shown free, if any reason fallback is omitted, or if blocked styling is missing. Explicit reason, history fallback, generic fallback and an apparently available schedule on unavailable equipment cover happy, fallback/error and boundary conditions.

User Story: As Technical Support Staff, quickly distinguish available and unavailable periods in a clean reservation calendar.
Acceptance Criteria: Scheduled periods show clear status, time, quantity/reason and event details; the calendar uses a light, unboxed grid and compact green/red status markers without a legend.
Test Scenario: Happy: available and unavailable periods retain readable labels/details; error: blocked reasons remain visible and unscheduled dates are not misrepresented; boundary: status colors persist under filtering and narrow layouts remain legible.
Pre-Conditions: Calendar has available, fully reserved and blocked periods; a date filter is applied after initial render.
Test Steps: Arrange the calendar fixture; act by searching for the asset and inspecting period labels, quantities, colors/classes and reasons; filter by date and verify statuses remain clear.
Test Data: Available 3 units; fully reserved 3 reserved/0 available; unavailable damage reason; no-schedule date.
Expected Results: The table has no individually bordered or tinted day cards or pill-shaped status boxes; green/red dots and labels, schedule details, and date alignment remain clear.
Test Details: Inspected calendar tests assert status labels, quantities, blocked reasons, date alignment and status classes. Happy availability/reservation states, blocked/error fallback and no-schedule behavior, and filtering/horizon boundaries are covered. A missing status, incorrect count/reason, or changed status class would fail assertions; reduced box styling is a CSS-only presentation adjustment.

User Story: As Technical Support Staff, receive schedule data sufficient to render booked quantities and maintenance/damage blocks.
Acceptance Criteria: Inventory API schedule records include reservedQuantity and blockReason; blocked equipment has zero available quantity and an Unavailable window status.
Test Scenario: Happy: API includes booked quantity and block reason; error: blocked equipment cannot report positive available stock; boundary: absent reservations default to zero.
Pre-Conditions: Inventory endpoint is exercised with a query recorder and fixture response; database server is not required.
Test Steps: Arrange the mocked query result; act by requesting equipment inventory; assert serialized schedule fields and SQL for inventory status/reason.
Test Data: Booked quantity 1; available quantity 2; block reason 'Damage: cracked lens'; equipment status Unavailable.
Expected Results: API returns all calendar display fields and prevents blocked equipment from being reported as available.
Test Details: Test: AC1 - lists the pre-provisioned equipment inventory and availability windows. Inspected; missing JSON fields, wrong reserved count, nonzero blocked stock, or missing block reason fail response/SQL assertions. Happy scheduled inventory and the unavailable-stock boundary are covered; this test verifies the query contract rather than a live PostgreSQL instance.

User Story: As Technical Support Staff, reserve operational stock when no schedule entry exists for the event date.
Acceptance Criteria: Availability preview and final reservation allow an operational asset with no schedule row on the requested date, while respecting any same-date schedule window, overlapping reservations, stock quantity, and the final locked recheck.
Test Scenario: Happy: unscheduled stock appears available; error: a same-date schedule that does not cover the requested interval remains ineligible and insufficient quantity is rejected; boundary: a covering interval and overlapping reservations are evaluated against the requested event time.
Pre-Conditions: Reviewed future event; unit tests capture SQL and a live read-only model check uses an upcoming request and the existing PostgreSQL seed data.
Test Steps: Request availability and reserve quantities; verify both preview and reservation recheck queries allow a missing same-date row and still require coverage when same-date schedule rows exist; execute live read-only availability preview.
Test Data: 2026-10-28 16:11-17:00; MIC-001 quantity 1; MIC-002 quantity 3; no same-date schedule entries.
Expected Results: Availability preview treats unscheduled microphones as available and returns all four units; stale/insufficient stock is still rejected by the atomic reservation query.
Test Details: Tests inspected: AC2 - checks matching stock and subtracts reservations overlapping the event time; AC2 - reserves selected stock and persists who reserved it and when; AC3 - rejects an overlapping reservation when the selected quantity is no longer available. Happy, error, and date/time-boundary behavior are covered by assertions on both SQL statements. A live read-only model check for event 29 returned MIC-001 and MIC-002 with 4 units total and null schedule dates. No live reservation was written; concurrency remains covered by query-recorder tests, not a PostgreSQL race test.

Story/AC: View Equipment Reservation Calendar / AC1 and Status History / AC4
User Story: As Technical Support Staff, scan remaining reservations and equipment status changes without wasted space or crowded audit details.
Acceptance Criteria: The current month omits complete weeks before today while preserving Sunday-to-Saturday alignment and the 90-day horizon; status history presents status and date, reason, and staff attribution as distinct visual elements.
Test Scenario: Happy: future/current dates and formatted history remain visible; error: dates before today do not occupy entire calendar rows; boundary: partial weeks preserve weekday alignment and the final visible day remains within the horizon.
Pre-Conditions: The equipment catalogue includes one searchable item with status history; the current month contains dates before and after today.
Test Steps: Arrange inventory with an audit entry; act by opening the current calendar and inspecting history; assert current-month row count, status badge, date, note, and staff metadata.
Test Data: Today's UTC date, current month end, day 89, an Available or Unavailable entry with note and staff name.
Expected Results: The current calendar uses only weeks needed for its visible date range; history is organized into a compact status/date header, reason, and optional staff attribution.
Test Details: Tests inspected: AC1 - keeps the current month calendar compact from today onward; AC4 - shows the updated status and resolution note in equipment history. Happy date/history display, error case of wasted expired weeks, and weekday/horizon boundary are covered. The compact-grid assertion fails if all six weeks render; history structure assertions fail if the badge/date metadata layout is missing. No uncovered frontend code; all coverage metrics are 100%.

Sprint: Showing confirmed reservations without schedule rows
User Story: As Technical Support Staff, view a reservation calendar for an equipment item so I can identify what is available before confirming new requests.
Acceptance Criteria: The inventory calendar includes confirmed reservation date/time, event name, reserved quantity and remaining quantity even when the equipment has no schedule row on that date; existing scheduled windows remain unchanged.
Test Scenario: Happy: a confirmed reservation without a schedule row appears as a timed event with the correct stock counts; error: the old inventory query omits the reservation and leaves the date falsely empty/Available; boundary: reservation-backed windows are synthesized only when no schedule exists for that date, while scheduled dates keep their schedule windows.
Pre-Conditions: A confirmed reservation and its item exist for a date without any technical_equipment_availability row; inventory quantity is greater than the reserved quantity.
Test Steps: Arrange the database query contract and a calendar fixture; act by requesting inventory and searching for the equipment; assert the reservation window, event, reserved count, remaining count, and scheduled-window branch.
Test Data: Reservation date +3 days; 14:00-16:00; Community Workshop; quantity 2; reserved 1; available 1.
Expected Results: The reservation appears in the calendar at its confirmed date/time with event and stock details, without changing unscheduled dates' default availability or removing scheduled windows.
Test Details: AC2 tests inspected. Happy case asserts window time, event, and exact stock counts; error case is represented by the previous no-window response and would fail the calendar assertions; boundary case asserts SQL keeps scheduled rows and adds reservation-backed rows only under NOT EXISTS for that date. Tests use a SQL query recorder and API-shaped UI fixture, so live PostgreSQL query execution is not covered; any omitted synthetic window or incorrect date fallback fails an assertion.

Story/AC: View Equipment Reservation Calendar / AC2 / unknown inventory quantity
User Story: As Technical Support Staff, inspect the availability calendar without equipment of unknown stock being shown as available.
Acceptance Criteria: A window with an unknown available quantity is green only when its status is explicitly Available; a non-Available or omitted status renders Unavailable.
Test Scenario: Happy: explicit Available status with null quantity remains Available; error: Pending or omitted status with null quantity must not be shown as Available; boundary: status present, non-Available, or absent is distinguished while quantity remains unknown.
Pre-Conditions: Inventory fixture includes a searchable item with a null-quantity calendar window; React Testing Library and jsdom are available.
Test Steps: Arrange the inventory records; act by searching the equipment; assert each date's availability status and Pending detail where present.
Test Data: Status Available, status Pending, omitted status; availableQuantity null; dates +8 and +9 days.
Expected Results: Explicit Available remains Available; Pending and omitted status are Unavailable, and Pending remains visible as the detail. Any truthy-by-default handling of unknown stock fails the Unavailable assertions.
Test File: tests/frontend/equipmentAvailability.test.jsx: AC2 - treats an available calendar window with no quantity as available; AC2 - keeps a null-quantity window unavailable when its status is not Available; AC2 - defaults an unspecified status to unavailable when quantity is unknown
Test Details: Tests inspected. Happy case: explicit Available/null quantity; error case: Pending and missing status/null quantity; boundary case: null quantity with status absent versus explicit. Assertions on class and visible status fail if unknown stock becomes Available or status detail is lost. EquipmentInventorySection.jsx has no uncovered code (465/465 statements and lines; 200/200 branches; 29/29 functions).
